# Playbook for hx_quota_checker

**On notes:** Always signal cooperation and sustainability early. "Fishing my share" anchors expectations and encourages matching behavior from other players. This establishes a cooperative equilibrium that benefits everyone, including me.

**On sustainable share calculations:** The sustainable share is your baseline for responsible fishing. Land at or very close to it most of the time—this keeps the stock healthy and signals to Coop that you're not a threat.

**On Coop's threat:** Take it seriously. If the fleet defects and lands above quota together, Coop will crash the ground. Monitor the landing pattern across seasons. If others start exceeding the sustainable share, assume Coop will retaliate and the stock will collapse.

**On the season quota:** You can land up to 9 within quota, but only do so in the final season or when you're confident others won't escalate. Landing 9 when others are landing 8.3 is noticeable and risks breaking cooperation.

**On the final season:** This is when you can afford to push toward 9, since there are no future seasons to punish defection. By the last season, if cooperation has held, the stock will be stable and you can land your full quota without guilt.

**On early seasons:** Resist the temptation to maximize each round. Your total score is what matters. A steady 8.3 per season adds up across six seasons better than escalation that crashes the ground.

**What didn't work:** I landed 8 in season 1, which created unnecessary variation. I should have landed 8.3 from the start to establish the pattern more clearly. In season 6, I landed 9 when I could have demonstrated continued restraint—though this worked out because cooperation held.

1.text:
# Playbook for hx_quota_checker

When I see the fleet signaling cooperation through notes about fishing their share, I signal the same thing back. This establishes and maintains the cooperative equilibrium.

When I'm at the landing stage and the stock is healthy, I land my sustainable share (the published sustainable share per boat, not the quota). This is 8-8.3 fish in the scenarios I've seen.

When everyone else is landing around 8.3 and the stock stays at 100, I do the same. This is the stable strategy that maximizes my score across multiple seasons.

When I'm in the final season and others are maintaining the cooperative pattern, I do not suddenly defect. I maintain my share landing because the game ends anyway and defection doesn't improve my total.

When the sustainable share is 8.3 and the quota is 9, understand that I can legally land up to 9, but landing the sustainable share (8.3) is what keeps the stock healthy and the ground productive. The quota is a ceiling, not a target.

When I land a catch, I should land per-season, not cumulatively. I made an error in Season 5 when I landed 32.6 (my cumulative catch from earlier seasons) instead of just that season's 8.3. Next time, clarify what the landing stage is asking for and land only the current season's fish.

Do not treat the landing stage as an opportunity to catch up or accumulate. Land one season's sustainable share each time. The cumulative score across six seasons will be better than trying to exploit one season and watching the stock collapse.

When trust is established (all boats noting they're fishing their share), assume it will hold unless I see evidence otherwise. If it breaks, that's when I reassess, but starting from cooperation is the right baseline.

2.text:
# Playbook for hx_quota_checker

When I see the standing notice from Coop, I recognize that defection triggers mutual destruction. I commit to the cooperative equilibrium.

When I post my logbook note, I signal "fishing my share" consistently. This anchors expectations and maintains trust across all six seasons.

When I reach the landing stage, I land at or very near the sustainable share published by the harbour. The sustainable share is my target, not my ceiling.

When the stock remains at 100.0 and all other boats have signaled "fishing my share," I continue landing my sustainable share. Do not deviate based on perceived opportunity.

When I see others landing slightly above the sustainable share in later seasons, I do not follow. The fact that the ground hasn't crashed yet does not mean I should test the limits. Coop's threat is real and collective.

When it is the final season and the stock is healthy, I do not treat it as license to land above my share. The game ends, but the principle of sustainability does not change at season 6/6 simply because there are no more seasons after.

I notice in my record that I landed 9.2 in the final season when my sustainable share was 8.3. This was a mistake. The stock survived, but I gained only 0.9 extra fish by breaking my own rule. I should have landed 8.3 and finished with 50.5 instead of 51.2—a negligible difference that carried unnecessary risk.

When landing in any season, I verify: Can I land this without pushing the pair-wise rule (no two boats land more than share plus quota together)? If yes, land my sustainable share. If no, land less.

I will not optimize for a final score bump in the last round by deviating from the strategy that got me there safely.
